newsitem.title: USA: Dollar falls on Japan/US concern about a weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls on Japan/US concern about a weak yen.

text.p: The dollar fell from a 4-1/2-year high vs. the yen Thursday after Japan's Finance Ministry and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said they were concerned about the dollar's rapid rise.
The dollar also declined against the German mark and other European currencies.
In Tokyo, the dollar rallied Thursday to 127.16 yen, its highest level since August 1992, before Japanese government officials warned the recent declines in the yen were too rapid and excessive.
Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying that recent yen moves were obviously excessive, which the market took as a warning that Japan would try to curb the dollar's rise.
The dollar also was knocked lower after Rubin said for the first time that the United States shared Japan's concern about the weak yen.

"They (Japan) are concerned ... about combatting excessive weakness with intervention and one can infer that he (Rubin) also shares their whole concern about the situation," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
The dollar fell to 125.85 yen from 126.80 on Wednesday.
Rubin, who spoke on CNBC television, stressed that the United States had not abandoned its policy of advocating a strong dollar, which initially gave the dollar a brief lift.
"Our policy is absolutely unchanged," Rubin said in answer to a question about the dollar and possible confusion in financial markets about U.S. policy.
Against the mark, the dollar shook off supportive comments from German finance officials, and fell to 1.7190 marks from 1.7255 marks on Wednesday.
"It's basically just following dollar/yen down," said Kisoo Park, a senior foreign exchange dealer at Bank of Boston.
Juergen Stark, the German State Secretary to the Finance Ministry said a dollar exchange rate over 1.72 marks was part of a normal correction from the dollar's record lows almost two years ago.
Meanwhile, Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said recent dollar moves were not sensational, given the relative strength of the U.S. economy compared with Germany.
In other trade, the dollar fell to 1.4685 Swiss francs from 1.4788 Swiss. It rose to Canadian $1.3937 from C$1.3895.
The British pound rose to $1.6230 from $1.6200.
